THE GAME, IN SHORT (check against GAME.md, do not take my summary as copy): SUPERCUT is a first-person roguelite puzzle shooter built in Unreal Engine 5.9 (C++). You carry a revolver and a clapperboard. A clap freezes the scene into a pencil sketch for a few seconds; charges are limited and carried from scene to scene, with pickups in the levels and rest rooms. Rooms are film sets; the enemies are wooden lay figures (Grunt, Rusher, Marksman). A perk card is offered after the first scene and then every third scene, with two rerolls per run. The run does not end at a last level: it goes on in laps until your health runs out. Levels are generated. Team name: [studio] Studios. Fonts in the game: Exo 2 Black Italic (display) and Saira Regular (text), both OFL. The build is Windows only; there is no web build.

WHAT THE OWNER WANTS FROM THIS THREAD: to design the itch.io page with him now, while the build is still being finished by other lanes. Likely pieces, in the order he chooses: page structure and copy (title line, short description, body, controls, how AI was used, credits pointer), the theme (colours, fonts, background, banner), cover image and screenshots, the download block, tags and metadata, the jam entry form's fields. Check itch.io's own documentation for sizes and limits (cover size, banner, what the theme editor allows, custom CSS needing approval) before you state one; do not quote sizes from memory.

Plain text for the itch.io entry form and the rules' required fields. No person's name, account or email:
`[owner fills]` marks those. Lines marked `[taste: owner review]` are wording choices.

## Team and people (rules 1(c), 5)

- Team name: [owner fills]
- Game name: SUPERCUT
- Team Owner, full name and email: [owner fills]
- Every other team member, full name and email: [owner fills]
- Student submission: [owner fills] (only if every member is enrolled at a higher-education institution)

## Build

- File: [owner fills: TeamName]_SUPERCUT.zip, the Windows Shipping package, one top folder, under 1 GB
- Platform: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, a DirectX 12 graphics card. Nothing to install: unzip and run `Supercut.exe`.
- Engine: Unreal Engine 5.9 (MegaJam Preview), C++.

## Gameplay video link

[owner fills] (30 to 60 s, 1920x1080 or higher, recorded gameplay, gameplay in the first 5 s)

## Dev log link (Glass Box)

[owner fills] (must open for the judges and be submitted with the entry before Mon 16 Nov 09:59 SGT)

## Game description `[taste: owner review]`

SUPERCUT is a first-person shooter set on a film set that fights back. You are the director. Snap your
clapperboard and the scene freezes: enemies, their shots and the machines stop where they are. Walk through the
frozen set, line up your shots (each one leaves the gun and hangs in the air), then let the scene roll and every
shot flies at once. Three snaps per room, four seconds each.

A run is one shooting day: a string of scenes, fights against wooden stand-in figures mixed with small puzzles
that need frozen time, like a wind machine you stop to slip past or marks that only show while the scene is
frozen. Between scenes you pick one of three upgrades. Die and it is "CUT!": the next take starts again from scene
one.

## How the theme is used (DIRECTOR'S CUT) `[taste: owner review]`

You play the director, and the clapperboard is your weapon. Every snap calls "CUT!" and stops the scene; the next
calls "ACTION!" and it plays out the way you set it up. Rooms are scenes, lives are takes ("SCENE 2, TAKE 3"), a
death is a cut, and the whole game takes place in a working film studio with lights, flats, cameras and crew
gear. Each run is your own cut of the day's shoot.

## Tools and AI used

The game was built during the jam by a small team working with AI coding agents.

The main thread confirmed controls, clap numbers and credits from the code on the `stack-lc` branch. Notes are in [LOG.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1/LOG.md>).

Three findings:
- **FORM_DRAFT's description is out of date.** It still says three snaps per room, a card after every scene and that death restarts at scene one, and it credits Roboto. I'll rewrite the description and controls rather than reuse them.
- **itch.io's docs give no size for the banner or background image.** They do give these: a cover at 315:250 (630x500 recommended), 3 to 5 screenshots of any size, and up to 10 tags. Custom CSS only comes after asking itch staff, so I'm planning without it.
- **Rule 15(d) covers the page art too.** No logos or trademarks except the Unreal Engine logo.

**Proposed page.** It uses itch's default two-column layout for downloadable games: the text on the left, with the video and screenshots in the sidebar.

1. **Banner:** the SUPERCUT title set in Exo 2 Black Italic. It replaces the plain title.
2. **Short description** (the line shown in listings), for example: "Clap the board, freeze the set, line up your shots, call action." `[taste: owner review]`
3. **Body:**
   - What the game is, in two sentences.
   - The clap: a 4 s pencil-sketch freeze, three charges carried between scenes, and shots that hang in the air until the scene rolls.
   - The run: generated scenes, a perk card after scenes 1, 4 and 7 with two rerolls, rest rooms, and laps until your health runs out.
   - The three wooden enemies.
4. **Controls:** taken from the key bindings in the code, with rebinding noted. Nothing about controllers.
5. **Download:** Windows 10/11 64-bit, unzip and run. The size stays a placeholder until main gives it.
6. **How it was made:** what the AI did and what people did, from SUBMISSION.md, with the dev log link for Glass Box.
7. **Credits:** a short list of sourced assets, with a pointer to the full CREDITS screen.

**Sidebar:** an empty slot for the video (it has to be a public YouTube or Vimeo link), then 3 to 5 real screenshots.

**Left out:** grenades, a web build, controller support and multiplayer. Grunt cover and the new stand models also stay out until they're proven.

**Decisions I need from you first:**

1. **The look.** Option A is a dark sound stage: near-black page, paper-white text, the player-shot yellow for links. Option B is pencil-sketch paper: off-white page, graphite text, echoing the freeze. Both use Exo 2 for headings and Saira for text. My pick is A, because the frozen screenshots would stand out against it. `[taste: owner review]`
2. **The cover.** Either a real frozen-scene screenshot with the title on it, or a real normal-play shot. My pick is the frozen shot. ```
## *Story*
*Cineruption* is a small puzzle-platformer set in a handmade paper world, built from papercraft, cardboard sets and the look of old cinema.
Cineruption: corruption, erupting all over cinema.
Something has gone terribly wrong behind the scenes. The Producer didn't like the film he paid for, so he cut out its heart and stuffed the holes with scenes of his own. When the Director asked for the missing scenes back, the Producer set the film vault on fire.
You are *Snip*, the stand-in nobody remembers. Take the scissors, put the Director's cut back together, and save the film before it all goes up in flames.
## *The scene is your level*
- *Cut* strips out of the film, sideways or up and down, and the world closes the gap
- *Splice* footage back in wherever it helps: stairs, ladders, a missing door
- *Rewind* time when a jump goes wrong
- *Double exposure:* be in two places at once to hold a plate down
## *Made like a film*
- Every scene starts with a *clapperboard*, and every fall is a *retake*: the takes are counted
- A *3-2-1 countdown leader* rolls before the film starts
- *Lamps hang from the rig*, so they stay put when you cut the film under them
- *Footage reels* keep every strip you cut, so you can splice it back in anywhere, along with the *deleted scenes* you find along the way
## *Controls*
Keyboard and mouse.
### *Moving*
- *← → or A / D*: run
- *Space*: jump (hold for a higher jump)
- *↑ ↓ or W / S*: climb ladders; at the top, Space or ↑ jumps off
### *Editing the film*
- *Drag across the film*: cut a strip out, sideways or up and down
- *Drag from a reel* (bottom of the screen) *into the film*: splice that footage in
### *Time*
- *Hold Z* (or the rewind wheel, bottom right): rewind time
- *← → while rewinding*: change the rewind speed (1x–8x)
- *Hold X*: double exposure, which leaves a ghost of yourself (stand still on the ground)
### *Other*
- *R*: retake the scene
- *Esc*: pause menu
- *M*: sound on / off
- *Enter or Space*: confirm in menus
*Goal:* collect every reel in the scene, then reach the door.
## *Technical disclosure*
Cineruption comes in two versions:
- *Browser (HTML5):* play it right here on this page. This is the main, most stable version.
- *Desktop (Unreal Engine, Windows):* a download that is still in development. It may have some visual inconsistencies and performance issues.
If you run into problems with the desktop version and still want to play, the browser version is the more s

draw at 2x, scale down for soft edges\n    layer = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (big, big), (0, 0, 0, 0))\n    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)\n    angle = math.radians(-62)  # close to the slant of the freeze's hatching\n    dx, dy = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)\n    for _ in range(26):  # stroke groups\n        cx, cy = rnd.uniform(0, big), rnd.uniform(0, big)\n        n = rnd.randint(4, 9)\n        length = rnd.uniform(40, 120)\n        gap = rnd.uniform(5, 9)\n        alpha = rnd.randint(60, 150)\n        for i in range(n):\n            ox = cx + i * gap * -dy + rnd.uniform(-2, 2)\n            oy = cy + i * gap * dx + rnd.uniform(-2, 2)\n            ln = length * rnd.uniform(0.6, 1.1)\n            for wx in (-big, 0, big):\n                for wy in (-big, 0, big):\n                    x0, y0 = ox + wx, oy + wy\n                    d.line(\n                        [(x0, y0), (x0 + dx * ln, y0 + dy * ln)],\n                        fill=GRAPHITE + (alpha,),\n                        width=rnd.choice((2, 2, 3)),\n                    )\n    layer = layer.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(0.6)).resize((TILE, TILE), Image.LANCZOS)\n    base = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (TILE, TILE), STAGE_BLACK + (255,))\n    # fine grain so the black is not flat\n    grain = Image.effect_noise((TILE, TILE), 6).convert(\"L\")\n    grain_rgba = Image.merge(\"RGBA\", (grain, grain, grain, grain.point(lambda v: 10)))\n    base = Image.alpha_composite(base, grain_rgba)\n    return Image.alpha_composite(base, layer).convert(\"RGB\")\n\n\ndef make_background() -> None:\n    frames = [hatch_frame(seed) for seed in (11, 12, 13, 14)]\n    frames[0].save(OUT / \"bg_tile.png\")\n    frames[0].save(\n        OUT / \"bg_tile.gif\", save_all=True, append_images=frames[1:], duration=180, loop=0, optimize=True\n    )\n\n\ndef make_banner() -> None:\n    w, h = 960, 250\n    img = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (w, h), (0, 0, 0, 0))\n    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)\n    # clapper stripe bar, slanted like the perk cards' top edge\n    bar_y, bar_h, stripe = 22, 26, 34\n    bar = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (w, bar_h), (20, 20, 22, 255))\n    bd = ImageDraw.Draw(bar)\n    for x in range(-bar_h, w + bar_h, stripe * 2):\n        bd.polygon([(x, bar_h), (x + stripe, bar_h), (x + stripe + bar_h, 0), (x + bar_h, 0)], fill=PAPER + (255,))\n    img.alpha_composite(bar, (0, bar_y))\n    font = ImageFont.truetype(str(FONT_DISPLAY), 150)\n    text = \"SUPERCUT\"\n    box = d.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)\n    tw = box[2] - box[0]\n    tx = (w - tw) // 2 - box[0]\n    ty = 66 - box[1]\n    d.text((tx + 6, ty + 6), text, font=font, fill=(0, 0, 0, 160))  # drop shadow\n    d.text((tx, ty), text, font=font, fill=PAPER + (255,))\n    img.save(OUT / \"banner.png\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    if not FONT_DISPLAY.is_file():\n        raise SystemExit(f\"missing font: {FONT_DISPLAY}\")\n    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n    make_background()\n    make_banner()\n    print(\"wrote\", sorted(p.name for p in OUT.iterdir()))\n"
}

Itch.io supports YouTube embeds in a game's description, though the exact method depends on whether you use the description editor or the trailer field.

- **Description editor:** A community answer says to use the editor's "Video" button to place a video in the description. Put a trailer in the page description if you want it near the top, and use the 'Video' button on the text editor. That post is from around 2,668 days ago, so the button may have moved.
- **Auto-embed by pasting a link:** Pasting a YouTube or Vimeo URL on its own line, then pressing Enter, should convert it to an embed. One guide says the link should be auto-embedded at that point. The same method works in comments and posts.
- **Trailer field:** The official docs say YouTube, Vimeo, and SketchFab links are supported. The docs place the video player in the secondary column, above the screenshots, so it is a separate spot from the description

cd "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1" && cat > tools/find_period.py <<'EOF'
"""Find a crop (rows y1..y2) of a generated background whose top row matches the row just below its bottom,
so the crop repeats down the page with no seam. Crop only: no pixel of the picture is changed.
Usage: python -I tools/find_period.py bg_gen2/bg_b.png"""
import sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

src = sys.argv[1]
a = np.asarray(Image.open(src).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32)
h = a.shape[0]
best = None
for y1 in range(0, h // 2):
    for y2 in range(y1 + 300, h):  # crop is rows y1..y2-1; the next copy's row y1 must match row y2
        d = np.abs(a[y1] - a[y2]).mean()
        # also compare a few rows on each side so a whole band matches, not one lucky row
        d += np.abs(a[y1 + 1:y1 + 4] - a[y2 + 1:y2 + 4]).mean() if y2 + 4 <= h else 99
        if best is None or d < best[0]:
            best = (d, y1, y2)
d, y1, y2 = best
raw = np.abs(a[0] - a[-1]).mean(axis=0)
crop = a[y1:y2]
join = np.abs(crop[-1] - crop[0]).mean(axis=0)
print(f"{src}: uncropped top/bottom diff RGB {raw.round(2)}; best crop y {y1}..{y2} (height {y2 - y1}); "
      f"crop bottom row vs top row RGB {join.round(2)}")
EOF
for n in a b c; do python -I tools/find_period.py bg_gen2/bg_$n.png; done
```

**Sun 15 Nov 23:24:31 · Tool call: Bash** (Draw a dev grid and composite it behind the scaffold)

```
cd "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1" && cat > tools/devgrid_composite.py <<'EOF'
"""Test: a white-and-grey prototype grid drawn by code, behind the scaffold of a cropped tile.
The scaffold is keyed off its white wall by brightness (the wall turns see-through; no pixel is painted in).
The grid's period divides the tile height, so the result still repeats with no seam.
Usage: python -I tools/devgrid_composite.py bg_gen2/bg_b_tile.png"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

src = Path(sys.argv[1])
tile = np.asarray(Image.open(src).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32)
h, w, _ = tile.shape
CELL = {300: 150, 315: 105}[h]   # big square; must divide the tile height
MINOR = CELL // 5

# grid: two-tone checker of big squares, minor lines, darker major lines; centred on the page's middle
y, x = np.mgrid[0:h, 0:w]
xc = x - w // 2
checker = ((xc // CELL) + (y // CELL)) % 2
grid = np.where(checker[..., None] == 0, 236.0, 222.0) * np.ones(3)
minor = (xc % MINOR == 0) | (y % MINOR == 0)
major = (xc % CELL == 0) | (y % CELL == 0) | (xc % CELL == 1) | (y % CELL == 1)
grid[minor] -= 14
grid[major] = 168

# key: how much darker than the wall each pixel is
lum = tile @ np.array([0.299, 0.587, 0.114])
wall = np.percentile(lum[:, w // 2 - 300:w // 2 + 300], 50)
alpha = np.clip((wall - 8 - lum) / 30.0, 0, 1)[..., None]
out = tile * alpha + grid * (1 - alpha)
dst = src.with_name(src.stem + "_devgrid.png")
Image.fromarray(out.clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(dst)
seam = np.abs(out[0] - out[-1]).mean()
print(f"wrote {dst} {w}x{h}, cell {CELL}, wall lum {wall:.1f}, top/bottom row diff {seam:.2f}")
t = Image.open(dst)
stack = Image.new("RGB", (w, h * 4))
for i in range(4):
    stack.paste(t, (0, i * h))
stack.resize((960, int(h * 4 * 960 / w))).save(src.with_name("stackgrid_" + src.stem[3:4] + ".jpg"), quality=88)
EOF
python -I tools/devgrid_composite.py bg_gen2/bg_b_tile.png && python -I tools/devgrid_composite.py bg_gen2/bg_c_tile.png
```

### Sun 15 Nov 23:25:13 · Agent (claude-opus-5-5)

Yes, it works. itch's theme editor takes only one background image, so I combined the two layers into one picture. The grid runs behind the scaffolding and the whole thing still repeats down the page.

Here are b + grid (left) and c + grid (right) at 1920 wide:

![grid behind scaffold](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1/shots/grid_bc_in_page.jpg>)

And a close-up of b + grid:

![close-up](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1/shots/grid_b_closeup.jpg>)

**How it's made:**
- **The grid is drawn by code:** large squares in two light greys, a fine grid inside each square, and darker lines at the square edges. That keeps it exact and ours.
- **The grid square divides the tile's height exactly**, so the pattern lines up from one tile to the next and still repeats with no join.
- **The scaffold is lifted off its white wall by brightness:** the wall becomes see-through and the grid shows behind it.
- **The wall's soft shadows from the scaffold are carried onto the grid**, so the steel doesn't look pasted on.
- I looked at the repeating stacks and the close-up. The grid is continuous across joins and there's no white fringe around the steel.

**Two things for you:**
- **It edits the generated picture a little.** Making the white wall see-through changes the picture's pixels. Nothing is painted in, but it's close to our no-edit rule for generated pictures. If you'd rather not, the other route is a fresh Codex generation of scaffolding in front of a grid wall. A generator is unlikely to draw a straight grid that repeats cleanly, though.
- **No numbers on the grid.** Real prototype grids often carry size labels like "512". I left them off. They're easy to add if you want them. `[taste: owner review]`

To compare, the mock's top bar has "b+grid" and "c+grid" next to the plain versions: [mock.html](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1/mock.html>). The script is [devgrid_composite.py](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1/tools/devgrid_composite.py>).

My pick is b + grid: the steel boards sit cleanly over the grey squares. `[taste: owner review]`

### Mon 16 Nov 01:09:06 · Agent (claude-opus-5-5)

I was half wrong. I tested a live itch page that demonstrates which HTML tags survive:

- **The tag works.** itch keeps `<kbd>` (the HTML tag for keyboard keys) in a description. The demo page shows keys like Tab, Enter and Ctrl wrapped in it.
- **The pill shape does not come with it.** itch's own stylesheet (`game.css`, about 167 KB) has no style for `<kbd>`. A browser's default for `<kbd>` is just a monospace font, with no border and no background. That demo page styles its keys through its own custom CSS (underline and font size), not through anything itch provides.

There are three ways to get pills on the page:

1. **Ask itch for custom CSS.** itch turns on per-page CSS for a creator on request. With it, I can paste the exact rule from the mock (border, rounded corners, padding) and the keys look like they do now. But it depends on itch staff answering before 09:59, and we can't count on that.
2. **Key-cap pictures.** itch allows images in the description, so each key could be a small PNG in the game's font. It looks right without custom CSS, but there are 13 images to upload and place by hand. They also won't change colour with the theme or stay crisp when someone zooms.
3. **Keep bold, as it is now.** It works today with nothing to ask for.

My recommendation is to keep bold on the page, and put `<kbd>` around each bold key anyway. If itch grants custom CSS later, one rule turns them into pills with no copy changes. Until then, `<kbd>` only switches the keys to a monospace font, so the copy would wrap them only once the CSS exists.

Should I file the custom CSS request as a to-do for you? You'd send it from your itch account, since I don't sign in.

- [itch.io forum post on the default HTML filter](https://itch.io/post/2408131)

   - Default is OFF (SupercutUserSettings.cpp 23).
   - The row is greyed where NVIDIA's plugin reports that DLSS Super Resolution cannot run on the PC (Row.Enabled = SupercutDlss::IsSupported).    - Credit wording stays plain text "NVIDIA DLSS"; no NVIDIA logo or badge art on the page.

rec = set(re.findall(r'"([a-z_]+)"', src.split("RECORDED = frozenset(")[1].split("})")[0]))
names = [p.stem for p in pathlib.Path("Audio/wav").glob("sc_*.wav")]
base = {re.sub(r"_\d$", "", n[3:]) for n in names}
nogren = {b for b in base if not b.startswith("grenade")}
r = nogren & rec; c = nogren - rec
print("distinct sounds (no grenade):", len(nogren), "recorded:", len(r), "code-made:", len(c))
print("code-made:", sorted(c))
EOF
```

d = nd.uniform_filter(np.abs(A - C).sum(axis=2), 5)

img.save(OUT + "cover_try3_big.png")

cd "D:/UE/Builds/pagepics1/cover" && python -I - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
A = np.asarray(Image.open("cover_C2+0.600.png").convert("L")).astype(float)
# slate (light) to bottom band (dark) edge, and slate top edge under the clapper stripes, scanned per column
def edge(y0, y1, light_above=True):
    pts = []
    for x in range(640, 1240, 20):
        col = A[y0:y1, x]
        g = np.diff(col)
        i = np.argmin(g) if light_above else np.argmax(g)
        pts.append((x, y0 + i))
    xs, ys = np.array(pts).T
    k, b = np.polyfit(xs, ys, 1)
    res = ys - (k * xs + b)
    return np.degrees(np.arctan(k)), np.abs(res).max(), pts[:3], pts[-3:]
print("bottom band top edge:", edge(650, 760, True))
EOF
```

lab, n = nd.label(m)

cd "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1" && python -I - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage as nd
F = "D:/UE/Builds/pagepics1/cover/"
A = np.asarray(Image.open(F+"cover_C2+0.600.png").convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32)
C = np.asarray(Image.open(F+"cover_C2+1.000.png").convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32)
dist = np.sqrt(((A - C) ** 2).sum(axis=2))
fg = nd.median_filter(dist, 7) > 14
lab, n = nd.label(fg); fg = lab == 1 + np.argmax(nd.sum(fg, lab, range(1, n + 1)))
fg = nd.binary_fill_holes(nd.binary_opening(nd.binary_closing(fg, iterations=2), iterations=2))
fg = nd.gaussian_filter(fg.astype(np.float32), 2.0) > 0.5
fg = nd.binary_erosion(fg, iterations=1)
paper_in = fg & (dist < 8)
ys, xs = np.nonzero(paper_in)
print("paper-like px inside mask:", paper_in.sum())
lab2, n2 = nd.label(paper_in)
sz = nd.sum(paper_in, lab2, range(1, n2+1)); com = nd.center_of_mass(paper_in, lab2, range(1, n2+1))
big = sorted(zip(sz, com), reverse=True)[:12]
for s, (cy, cx) in big: print(int(s), int(cx), int(cy))
# how far from the mask edge are they
edge_d = nd.distance_transform_edt(fg)
print("distance from edge pct", np.percentile(edge_d[paper_in], [50, 90, 99]).round(1))
EOF

al = nd.gaussian_filter(fg.astype(np.float32), 0.8)
comp = B * (1 - al[..., None]) + A * al[..., None]
for name, (x0, y0, x1, y1) in {"forearm": (380, 560, 640, 962), "thumb": (760, 200, 960, 330)}.items():
    im = Image.fromarray(comp[y0:y1, x0:x1].clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8))

```
"""Page art for the SUPERCUT itch.io page (lane itch1).

Writes into ../art/:
  banner.png    transparent banner: clapper stripes and the title in the game's own Exo 2 Black Italic

Run: python -I tools/make_page_art.py   (from the lane folder)
Colours are sampled from the game's own screenshots (see LOG.md, 15 Nov 22:4x).
"""
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

LANE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = LANE / "art"
FONT_DISPLAY = Path("D:/UE/Projects/Supercut59/Art/fonts/exo2/Exo2-BlackItalic.ttf")

PAPER = (240, 236, 225)


def make_banner() -> None:
    w, h = 960, 250
    img = Image.new("RGBA", (w, h), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    # clapper stripe bar, slanted like the perk cards' top edge
    bar_y, bar_h, stripe = 18, 34, 34
    bar = Image.new("RGBA", (w, bar_h), (20, 20, 22, 255))
    bd = ImageDraw.Draw(bar)
    for x in range(-bar_h, w + bar_h, stripe * 2):
        bd.polygon([(x, bar_h), (x + stripe, bar_h), (x + stripe + bar_h, 0), (x + bar_h, 0)], fill=PAPER + (255,))
    img.alpha_composite(bar, (0, bar_y))
    font = ImageFont.truetype(str(FONT_DISPLAY), 150)
    text = "SUPERCUT"
    box = d.textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    tw = box[2] - box[0]
    tx = (w - tw) // 2 - box[0]
    ty = 66 - box[1]
    d.text((tx + 6, ty + 6), text, font=font, fill=(0, 0, 0, 160))  # drop shadow
    d.text((tx, ty), text, font=font, fill=PAPER + (255,))
    bottom = ty + box[3] + 6 + 18  # title's lowest pixel, its shadow, and an 18 px margin
    img.crop((0, 0, w, bottom)).save(OUT / "banner.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if not FONT_DISPLAY.is_file():
        raise SystemExit(f"missing font: {FONT_DISPLAY}")
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    make_banner()
    print("wrote", sorted(p.name for p in OUT.iterdir()))
(960, 198)
```

Its region touching the frame's lower right is dropped from A's mask.\ny, x = np.mgrid[0:1080, 0:1920]\nneutral = m_A & (np.abs(A[..., 0] - A[..., 2]) < 15) & (x > 1150) & (y > 600)\nlab, n = nd.label(nd.binary_closing(neutral, iterations=3))\ngun = np.isin(lab, [i for i in range(1, n + 1) if (lab == i)[CROP[3] - 40:, CROP[2] - 120:].any()])\nboard = m_A & ~nd.binary_dilation(gun, iterations=2)\nboard = nd.binary_closing(board, iterations=2)   # fills the 1 px seam between the clap stick and the slate\nlab, n = nd.label(board)\nboard = lab == 1 + np.argmax(nd.sum(board, lab, range(1, n + 1)))\nboard = nd.binary_fill_holes(board)\n\n\ndef layer_alpha(m):\n    \"\"\"Soft alpha inside a hard mask: one pixel in (the beauty's own edge pixels blend with the world behind),\n    then a 0.7 px feather.\"\"\"\n    return nd.gaussian_filter(nd.binary_erosion(m, iterations=1).astype(np.float32), 0.7)\n\n\ndef outline(img, m):\n    \"\"\"Glow then stroke outside the mask, under the layer.\"\"\"\n    if not STYLES[STYLE]:\n        return img\n    s_col, s_w, g_col, g_reach, g_str = STYLES[STYLE]\n    out_d = nd.distance_transform_edt(~nd.binary_erosion(m, iterations=1))   # px outside the layer's edge\n    glow = g_str * np.exp(-np.maximum(out_d - s_w, 0) / (g_reach / 3)) * (out_d > 0)\n    img = img * (1 - glow[..., None]) + np.array(g_col, np.float32) * glow[..., None]\n    stroke = np.clip(s_w + 0.5 - out_d, 0, 1)\n    return img * (1 - stroke[..., None]) + np.array(s_col, np.float32) * stroke[..., None]\n\n\nright = np.clip((x - (900 - (y - 540) * 0.25)) / 3.0 + 0.5, 0, 1)\ncomp = B * (1 - right[..., None]) + G * right[..., None]\ncomp = outline(comp, board)\na = layer_alpha(board)\ncomp = comp * (1 - a[..., None]) + A * a[..., None]\n\n# the slate: between the stripe bar's lower edge and the dark band's upper edge, between the board's sides,\n# measured in A. The slate is one even cream run (about 225) per row; take the longest bright run in each slate\n# row and the median of its ends.\nL = A.mean(axis=2)\nsides = []\nfor row in range(540, 680, 10):\n    bright = nd.uniform_filter1d(L[row, 450:1400], 5) > 195\n    lab1, n1 = nd.label(bright)\n    big = 1 + np.argmax(nd.sum(bright, lab1, range(1, n1 + 1)))\n    xs = np.nonzero(lab1 == big)[0] + 450\n    sides.append((xs.min(), xs.max()))\nleft, right_edge = np.median([s[0] for s in sides]), np.median([s[1] for s in sides])\nmid_x = int(round((left + right_edge) / 2))\n\n\ndef edge_at(xc, y_from, y_to, dark_above):\n    col = nd.uniform_filter1d(L[y_from:y_to, xc - 6:xc + 7].mean(axis=1), 3)\n    g = np.diff(col)\n    return y_from + (np.argmax(g) if dark_above else np.argmin(g))\n\n\ntop = edge_at(mid_x, 400, 560, True)       # stripe bar (dark) above, slate below\nbottom = edge_at(mid_x, 620, 760, False)   # slate above, dark band below\nmid_y = (top + bottom) / 2\nxs = np.arange(int(left) + 40, int(right_edge) - 40, 20)\nys = np.array([edge_at(int(v), 620, 760, False) for v in xs])\ntilt = float(np.degrees(np.arctan(np.polyfit(xs, ys, 1)[0])))\nprint(f\"board sides x {left:.0f}..{right_edge:.0f}, slate y {top}..{bottom} at x {mid_x}, tilt {tilt:.2f} deg\")\n\n# the logo, in full-frame coordinates, onto the board\nlogo = Image.open(LOGO)\nys_, xs_ = np.nonzero(np.asarray(logo)[..., 3])\nlogo = logo.crop((xs_.min(), ys_.min(), xs_.max() + 1, ys_.max() + 1))   # its ink box\nlogo = logo.resize((LOGO_W, round(logo.height * LOGO_W / logo.width)), Image.LANCZOS)\nlayer = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (1920, 1080), (0, 0, 0, 0))\nlayer.paste(logo, (round(mid_x - logo.width / 2), round(mid_y - logo.height / 2)))\nlayer = np.asarray(layer.rotate(-tilt, resample=Image.BICUBIC, center=(mid_x, mid_y))).astype(np.float32)\nla = layer[..., 3:] / 255\ncomp = comp * (1 - la) + layer[..., :3] * la\n\n# the sketched revolver and hand in front of everything\ncomp = outline(comp, m_G)\na = layer_alpha(m_G)\ncomp = comp * (1 - a[..., None]) + G * a[..., None]\n\nx0, y0, x1, y1 = CROP\nout = Image.fromarray(comp[y0:y1, x0:x1].clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8))\n(LANE / \"cover\").mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nout.resize((630, 500), Image.LANCZOS).save(LANE / f\"cover/cover_v7_{STYLE}_630x500.png\")\nout.resize((315, 250), Image.LANCZOS).save(LANE / f\"cover/cover_v7_{STYLE}_315x250_check.png\")\n# close-ups for checking: the left hand's edge over the normal set, and the revolver over the board\nout.crop((0, 120, 420, 850)).save(LANE / f\"shots/cover_v7_{STYLE}_hand_left.png\")\nout.crop((700, 300, 1071, 850)).save(LANE / f\"shots/cover_v7_{STYLE}_right.png\")\nprint(f\"wrote cover/cover_v7_{STYLE}_630x500.png\")\n"
}

### Mon 16 Nov 04:22:56 · Agent (claude-opus-5-5)

Only partly. itch has no font picker in the description editor. The page theme sets one font for headings and one for body text, and the editor strips most inline styling. An itch staff post says inline CSS is limited to "a few simple properties", and other users say a `font-family` style gets removed when you save. Changing fonts per element needs custom CSS, and itch only turns that on if you ask its support, which won't happen before the deadline.

What you can do midline:
- **Bold and italic.** These always work. "Code:" and the other labels are already bold.
- **Monospace** with `<code>`, for example `Code:`. It reads as code text, which suits the Code label but looks odd on 2D and Sound.
- **Colour** with `<span style="color:…">`. Users report this works and staff named it as one of the allowed properties, but it's not confirmed. You'd need to test it in the draft preview before relying on it.

If what you want is labels that look like the headings (Exo 2, heavy italic), the closest you can get is bold italic in the body font, optionally in the page's link yellow. I'd do that, and we test the colour in the draft before it goes live. `[taste: owner review]` Want me to mock it up that way?

Sources:
- [itch.io staff on inline CSS](https://itch.io/post/2408131)
- [itch.io CSS guide](https://itch.io/docs/creators/css-guide)
- [Custom CSS on itch pages](https://medium.com/the-bkpt/how-to-use-custom-css-on-itch-io-pages-5d00b207bc)
- [itch forum: HTML in descriptions](https://itch.io/post/2287401)

1. Not generated at play time. The rooms are made ahead of time by our Python room generator (`Tools/gen`), checked there, and baked into text room files; the game reads them like any room file. What IS random at play time: which baked run you get, the perk cards offered, health drops and the rest rooms, all from the run's seed.
2. 12 runs ship (seeds 1 to 12, 12 rooms each; the repo has 50 baked, the entry keeps 12 because `GeneratedRuns = 12`). One is picked when the GAME IS LAUNCHED, from the clock: run `gen_s<1 + seed % 12>`. It is not re-picked inside one launch: QUIT TO TITLE and START play the same run again.
3. A second take after a death plays the same rooms again from scene 1 (same run, perks lost; the card offers carry on from the same random stream, so they can differ). RESTART RUN from the pause menu replays the same run with the same card offers from the start. Clearing a run's 12th room does not end the game: it rolls on into the NEXT baked run (seed + 1, wrapping at 12), entered at that run's room 5, with enemies scaled up per lap; ENDLESS MODE begins at scene 11 either way.

So an honest line is "levels built by our procedural generator: 12 runs of 12 rooms, one picked each time you launch", not "procedurally generated as you play". The "50-run" mention in GAME.md is the number baked in the repo, not what ships.

The main thread checked this in the code. The levels are procedurally generated, but ahead of time, not while you play:
- **How they're made:** our Python generator built the runs and checked each one, and they ship as baked room files.
- **What ships:** 12 runs of 12 rooms each. The repo holds 50, so the "50" in the notes isn't what players get.
- **How one is picked:** the game picks a run when you launch it, based on the clock. You keep the same run until you quit the game. Dying, quitting to the title screen or restarting from the pause menu all replay that same run.
- **What changes on a retake:** after a death, the perk cards you're offered can be different.
- **After room 12:** the game moves on to the next run, starting at its room 5, with tougher enemies.

So "no two takes play out the same" is out: a second take is the same rooms. Two honest options:

2. **More detail:** "The sets come from our own procedural level generator: 12 shoots of 12 scenes, one picked at random each time you launch. Clear one and the next rolls in, harder."

**Roguelike or roguelite:** by how the terms are used now, SUPERCUT is a roguelike, not a roguelite.
- **Roguelite** usually means something carries over between runs: unlocks, currency, permanent upgrades.
- **SUPERCUT** carries nothing over. When you die you lose every perk and start again at scene 1, and the game notes say "No progress carries between runs".
- **The catch:** for purists, a strict roguelike is turn-based on a grid, which this isn't. "Action roguelike" is the label nobody can argue with.

My suggestion is to change "roguelite" to "roguelike" in The set ("SUPERCUT is a roguelike first-person shooter…") and swap the tag Roguelite for Roguelike. If you want to be fully precise, write "action roguelike" in the text, but that makes the opening line longer. `[taste: owner review]`

The towers already repeat every 192 px, which makes a seamless loop easy. A plain CSS animation isn't an option: itch only allows custom CSS after you ask its support, and that won't happen before the deadline.

**The problem.** Users on itch's forums report that animated GIFs uploaded as a page background or banner stop animating. itch serves only the first frame, as a tiny still image. The latest reports I found are from late 2025, and I found no sign it's been fixed. Earlier pages did have working GIF backgrounds, so it did work at some point.

**Why it's low risk anyway.** If itch freezes the GIF, visitors see frame 1, and frame 1 would be exactly the current background. Nothing breaks if it fails. The costs:
- An upload of roughly 2 to 5 MB instead of 101 KB.
- Possible colour banding in the grey from the GIF's limited colours.
- Constant motion behind the text, which some readers find distracting.

**My take:** worth a try only if you're already editing the itch draft and can test it there. I'd keep the motion slow, about one 192 px repeat every 6 to 8 seconds. Want me to make it? `[taste: owner review]`

### Mon 16 Nov 07:45:39 · Agent (claude-opus-5-5)

Yes. On itch you build the game's page first, as its own project, and then submit that project to the jam. Doing it as a draft is fine, because only you can see a draft until you publish it.

It's 07:45 and the deadline is 09:59, so start with the upload. The 638 MB zip will take a while.

**1. Create the project**
Go to itch.io, then Dashboard, then **Create new project**, and fill in the edit page. Here's where each part of the mock goes:

| Field | What to enter |
| --- | --- |
| Title | SUPERCUT |
| Classification / Kind | Game, Downloadable |
| Release status | In development |
| Pricing | No payments |
| Uploads | `D:\UE\Builds\entry_f6\[studio]_SUPERCUT.zip`, with **Windows** ticked |
| Description | Copy it section by section from the mock. Put the trailer link on its own line at the top. |
| Genre, Tags, AI disclosure | As in the mock's More information block |
| Cover image | [cover_v8_white_630x500.png](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1/cover/cover_v8_white_630x500.png>) |
| Gameplay video | https://[video-site].be/NiNL1RUXLBE |
| Screenshots | The stills from `stills/` |
| Visibility | **Draft** for now |

Then press Save.

**2. Theme the page**
Open the saved page and click **Edit theme** in the bar at the top. Set the banner ([banner.png](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1/art/banner.png>)), the background (the moving GIF) and the colours and fonts from [THEME.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/itch1/THEME.md>). While you're there, check that the GIF moves and that the trailer plays.

**3. Submit to the jam**
On https://itch.io/jam/2026-epic-ai-megajam, press **Submit your project** and pick SUPERCUT. Fill in the jam's own questions from the main thread's [FORM_DRAFT.md](<[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/submit1/FORM_DRAFT.md>): names and emails, the Team Owner, sourced assets, tools and AI used, and the dev log. Then you press Submit. The rules (section 17) say a person has to do that.

**Draft or public?** The rules say the entry must be "directly accessible by Sponsor". As far as I know, itch hides a draft from the jam's entries until it's public. I haven't checked that on the live site, so set the page to **Public** before 09:59 to be safe. You can keep editing it afterwards.

Two things to delete when you paste the description:
- the yellow review bar at the top of the mock
- the "List checked against SUBMISSION.md" line

The dev log link stays out until the repo opens for visitors.

If you're already signed in to itch in your browser, I can fill the draft fields you name, one save at a time, and tell you before each save. I won't sign in, publish or submit.

from PIL import Image

You alone are the director, and rogue mannequins have overrun your set. <strong>With only a revolver and a clapperboard, it's your job to take them all down.</strong></p>\n<p>Clap the board and the scene freezes into a pencil sketch. Fire into the freeze and every shot hangs in the air until the scene rolls again. There is no end to the madness... the shoot goes on until you die.</p>\n<p>IMGGIF</p>\n<h2>Cut » Action</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Clap the board</strong> and the scene freezes into a pencil sketch.</li>\n<li><strong>Shoot during the freeze.</strong> Your bullets hang in the air.</li>\n<li><strong>Action.</strong> Watch the mannequins fall as time unfreezes.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>IMGROW</p>\n<h3 style=\"text-align: center;\">WATCH your charges... They are limited.</h3>\n<h2>Rewrites &amp; Last Rites</h2>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Pick a perk.</strong> Every few scenes, pick one of three perks, or reroll for a new hand.</li>\n<li><strong>Shifting sets.</strong> Scenes are procedurally generated, so be wary of every angle.</li>\n<li><strong>Endless Mode.</strong> Past scene 10, there are no more perks, and one hit will kill you.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>IMGPAIR</p>\n<h2>Controls</h2>\n<p>Keyboard and mouse. Every key can be rebound in the settings, with a fully fledged menu to customize everything.</p>\n<h3>Movement</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>W</strong> <strong>A</strong> <strong>S</strong> <strong>D</strong> move, <strong>Space</strong> jump, mouse to look</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Shooting</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Left mouse</strong> fire, <strong>R</strong> reload</li>\n<li><strong>Right mouse</strong> clap to freeze the scene</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Perk cards</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>1</strong> <strong>2</strong> <strong>3</strong> or click a card to pick it, <strong>R</strong> or the button to reroll</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Other</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Esc</strong> pause: settings, controls, credits, quit</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Download</h2>\n<p><strong>Windows 10 / 11, 64-bit. We built SUPERCUT during the jam in Unreal Engine 5.9 (C++), working with AI agents. This is our first Unreal Engine project, and it was a blast to work in. 76 hours of non-stop work, <strong>over 135 agents</strong> deployed, <strong>6.7 billion tokens</strong> processed.</p>\n<h3>What agents did</h3>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Code:</strong> Claude Fable 5.2 ran as the orchestrator and handed the work to 136 agents on Fable 5.2 for open-ended work, Opus 5.5 for well-scoped tasks, and Sonnet 5.5 for playtesting and code reading.</li>\n<li><strong>3D:</strong> GPT 6 Astra made reference pictures with GPT Images 2.6, and agents turned them into the props, the revolver and the clapperboard through Hyper3D Rodin. 3204

Cut. Shoot. Action.
The set

SUPERCUT is a roguelike first-person shooter on a movie studio's bare film set. You alone are the director, and rogue mannequins have overrun your set. With only a revolver and a clapperboard, it's your job to take them all down.

Clap the board and the scene freezes into a pencil sketch. Fire into the freeze and every shot hangs in the air until the scene rolls again. There is no end to the madness... the shoot goes on until you die.

Cut » Action

    Clap the board and the scene freezes into a pencil sketch.
    Shoot during the freeze. Your bullets hang in the air.
    Action. Watch the mannequins fall as time unfreezes.

WATCH your charges... They are limited.
Rewrites & Last Rites

    Pick a perk. Every few scenes, pick one of three perks, or reroll for a new hand.
    Shifting sets. Scenes are procedurally generated, so be wary of every angle.
    Endless Mode. Past scene 10, there are no more perks, and one hit will kill you.

Controls

Keyboard and mouse. Every key can be rebound in the settings, with a fully fledged menu to customize everything.
Movement

    W A S D move, Space jump, mouse to look

Shooting

    Left mouse fire, R reload
    Right mouse clap to freeze the scene

Perk cards

    1 2 3 or click a card to pick it, R or the button to reroll

Other

    Esc pause: settings, controls, credits, quit

Download

Windows 10 / 11, 64-bit. Unzip and run Supercut.exe in the SUPERCUT folder, no install or internet connection needed.sho

How it was made

[studio] Studios is a two-person studio. We built SUPERCUT during the jam in Unreal Engine 5.9 (C++), working with AI agents. This is our first Unreal Engine project, and it was a blast to work in. 76 hours of non-stop work, over 135 agents deployed, 6.7 billion tokens processed.
What agents did

    Code: Claude Fable 5.2 ran as the orchestrator and handed the work to 136 agents on Fable 5.2 for open-ended work, Opus 5.5 for well-scoped tasks, and Sonnet 5.5 for playtesting and code reading.
    3D: GPT 6 Astra made reference pictures with GPT Images 2.6, and agents turned them into the props, the revolver and the clapperboard through Hyper3D Rodin. Agents built the remaining set in Blender.
    2D: GPT 6.1 Sol and GPT 6 Astra drew the perk and HUD icons with GPT Images 2.6. The particle and sketch textures were drawn by code.
